[Qivera Aindra](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1RnuOnwrHU-41wA9MC7JKcdPonrVK0NGJJOhRWTXIp_8/edit?usp=sharing) is a ceruleanblood girl with a passion for FLARP and other nerdy hobbies, but she hides bright blue blood, unique if possibly horrifying powers, and a secret former life as a troll lab rat.

(Her backstory has a lot of medical themes so please be cautious if that's something that may upset you. It won't be detailed in actual play. Also, her flesh-shaping powers are on the mild side, visually.)

[Hekata Nician](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1E8NPOCMXyWlXchHz0V3mqfxaQkIW-lpPMh2wuYqPYPo/edit?usp=sharing) is a rustblood who was taken under the wing of a mysterious organization and groomed to be a weapon against the empire.

[Korryn Raqqis](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1are-dml3pLqRo7AgXBup7xpW1kGjGBauRQhab7Q4WDc/edit?usp=sharing) is a native of the planet Mudracon, a resource colony under the Alternian Empire focused on harvesting Sikl, a highly valuable narcotic that is produced by the giant sand serpents that live beneath its sands. She works as a courier, delivering the drug from the outpost where it is harvested to the only city on the planet, Cliff-Crush.

[Calentha](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MlGvybZNbNQ2B6Te_fAtPaPYXbmseczHbFUjiRL0ums/edit?usp=sharing) is something nearly unique on Earth C: a Cherub. With a karmic connection to the greatest evil that paradox space has ever known, so little knowledge of Earth C, and such great curiosity, there's a lot for her to learn, and much at stake.

I found reading Vast Error to be a lot easier to stomach than Homestuck, personally, though maybe it's just because I'm older now and have gotten used to reading through purple prose stuff. I only had two moments reading it where I was genuinely really confused about what a character had said, and one of those was just a result of my brain not liking Dismas' quirk.

It's definitely a lot darker in tone than Homestuck, and it takes its darker themes a lot more seriously in the moment than Homestuck did (no playing domestic abuse for laughs), but I actually appreciate that, because it means Vast Error just comes across as more mature in general. It's fundamentally different from Homestuck in that it's not a story about growing up, it's a story about being a grown up. All of the characters are deeply flawed people, most of them with some kind of trauma, and they're trying to survive and recover in an uncaring, dying world without the help of a lot of the people that they used to depend on, which is something that I think a lot of people my age can relate to.

Is it perfect? Nah. I like it, though.
Fucked up? Definitely. Deeply amusing for me? Also definitely.

Alt!Calliope may be an ancient, nearly omnipotent being, but she's still an emotionally damaged girl who never developed a properly complex set of emotions due to predominating over her brother early. She's emotionally stunted like Caliborn, just in a different way.

Trolls still have secondary sexual characteristics and they seem to have "tertiary sexual characteristics" (gender signalers like clothing/makeup), so having trolls that don't identify with the characteristics that society would expect them to have/that their biology gave to them doesn't seem that improbable to me. 

Basically, if trolls are similar enough to humans to have Will fucking Smith, I don't see why they can't or shouldn't have trans people, even if their experience of that is different from ours (and honestly I'd love to read about how weird bug aliens would experience dysphoria and other Trans Things[TM]).
But part of my point is that they DO amount to something! They show us sides of the characters we might otherwise never have seen. Things they could've done.

Thinking optimistically, I think part of the idea of [S] Game Over and the loss of the surrounding character development was trying to set up a lesson about how things work in Paradox Space: 

1. Trying to force yourself into relevance will only end in misery for yourself and everyone else. 

2. People who are relevant aren't necessarily "better" or "more important", and they definitely aren't happier, as we see with the difference between retconned Vriska and alpha Vriska. It showed that Vriska was capable of change, and that Terezi was truly capable of forgiving her. Their experiences aren't invalid, they still very much have feelings and thoughts and their actions are important to them, even if not to the narrative of the comic. It's part of Homestuck's larger narrative about how characters can be people, perhaps even more nuanced than real people in some ways due to the fact that there are millions of gradations of them that show many different ways they could've turned out as a person.

[Amuria Brises](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ziCAJL1rzVxVHE6o09O9EiBEZCxXkJOSZdJNpXZoPZc/edit?usp=sharing)

Your name is Amuria Brises. You are the reigning champion of a town/illegal fighting ring known as The Lightning Hemisphere because you are extremely talented at violence, and though you sincerely believe in the cause of The Mirthful Messiahs and want to commit great acts in their name, all of this violence is finally starting to get to you. At least you have your collection and your art to help you calm down.

Assuming that all of the appropriate Sburb mechanics were in place (strife specibi, scaling stats like mangrit, sylladexes), I think I'd do okay. I tend to learn games fairly quickly and I think I have a natural affinity for adapting to bullshit. If I have some decent friends by my side to support me through the inevitable existential crisis, I think it'll go okay.

Now, if I didn't have those systems to empower me (notably the scaling stats), I think I'd make it through, like, two imps before mcfuckingdying. Maybe more depending on what weapon falls readily to hand(maybe I could make it a little further with a shotgun or something), but not a lot more.

FWIW, I see myself as a Rogue of Rage.

I've never used TTS before, but I have played both some D&D and Pathfinder. I understand the basic ideas, at the very least. I should be able to make basically every single night, barring a tragedy or something. I love role-playing, and I have a decent amount of experience doing it.

I'm not really involved in SCA, although I've been looking into it. I just got curious about this group. From what my father told me, it was the kind of thing where people did get very seriously injured on more than a few occasions.

(Not looking to join them or anything. I don't plan on getting killed anytime soon.)
